linkedin.text:
Your provider's invoice says what you spent. It doesn't say which agent spent it.

In Control Tower every agent has its own key, and every call through the gateway is priced once, at the rate in force when it was routed. The Ledger adds it up: spend, requests, tokens and errors per agent and per model or tool server, for the last hour, day, week or month. Usage a provider didn't report is estimated and marked as such.

Then you can put a number on it. Budgets go on a key, a team or a project. A hard budget refuses the next call with 429 budget_exceeded; a soft one alerts instead. Every call is checked against every budget that covers it, so the tightest wins, and against what's already in flight, so a burst of parallel requests can't run far past the cap.

When one agent calls another, the spend counts against the agent that started the chain.

Open source and self-hosted: https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower. A ⭐ helps others find it.

#AIAgents #OpenSource #PlatformEngineering

posts:
Your provider's invoice tells you what you spent.

It doesn't tell you which agent spent it.

Control Tower's Ledger does: spend, tokens and errors per agent, team and model, every call priced at the rate in force when it was routed.

Then put a cap on it. Budgets per key, team or project.

Hard budget used up → the next call gets 429 budget_exceeded. Checked against what's already in flight, so parallel calls can't blow far past it.

Agent calls agent? Spend counts against the one that started the chain.

Open source, self-hosted, one docker run to try with a demo fleet.

A ⭐ helps other engineers find it: https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower
